page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i3g.2xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes 479 GB of bundled local SSD storage. Network performance is anchored by a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations show average performance across most standard operations. The server achieves an average Passmark CPU score of 8286.39 and a Passmark memory score of 2333.72. Multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng is average at 7006.17, though single-core stress-ng performance is weak at 1314.6. In data processing, the server handles Redis SET operations at an average rate of 6.88 million operations per second and delivers an average static web serving throughput of 6.92 GB/sec. However, it exhibits poor performance on larger workloads, such as LLM inference with a 7B model, which drops to 6.09 tokens per second for text generation.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.i3g.2xlarge offers a balanced resource density by combining dedicated Intel Xeon processing cores with a substantial 479 GB local SSD. This makes it a viable option for workloads requiring local storage without the overhead of external disk attachments. It is well-suited for general-purpose applications, software compilation, static web serving, and moderate database operations, though it is not recommended for intensive machine learning or heavy multi-threaded compute tasks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i3g.2xlarge is an x86_64 virtual server featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, paired with 32.0 GB of RAM and 479 GB of bundled local SSD storage. Operating on a KVM hypervisor, it delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps. Benchmark data indicates average performance across standard operations, including a Passmark CPU score of 8286.39 and a Redis SET throughput of 6.88 million operations per second. However, single-core CPU performance and multi-threaded decompression tasks are relatively weak. The inclusion of local SSD storage alongside balanced compute and memory resources makes this instance qualitatively cost-effective for workloads that require fast local disk access. It is best suited for general-purpose applications, static web serving, software compilation, and moderate database operations.
